minutes.headline: Water district heard a pilot-study plan for the Hickory Hills well; residents pressed on lake levels; cell lease and audit contract moved
minutes.summary: Consultants presented a preliminary scope for a roughly year-long pilot study of iron, manganese and PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills well, plus lake-level monitoring. Residents of The Woodlands and Hickory Hills raised concerns about truck traffic, trailer placement, discharge location, and whether the pilot would show any lake-level impact. The board also moved to sign a T-Mobile tower lease and the annual audit contract, and the pilot study is to return at the next meeting for final review.

what_happened.line: The board moved to sign a T-Mobile tower lease; the minutes record the motion but the vote count was not audible.
The board moved to sign the annual audit contract, renewed with the CPA with no change from prior years; the count was not audible.
Consultants presented a preliminary scope and schedule for a pilot study of iron, manganese and PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills well, with lake-level monitoring.
Residents raised trailer placement, truck traffic, discharge near the swim beach and whether the pilot tests lake-level impact; none was resolved.
The pilot study will return as an agenda item at the next meeting for final review, and a developer's water service request is referred to December 14.

why_it_matters: The pilot study is the step before any permanent treatment at the Hickory Hills well, and its siting, discharge and lake-level monitoring are what neighbors in The Woodlands and Hickory Hills are asking the district to settle first.
The tower lease brings the district an annual payment with a yearly escalator, and the audit contract continues unchanged, but the minutes do not record how members voted on either.
